name: Recode Studios
tagline: Makeup and cosmetics brand with its own retail stores
excerpt: Makeup brand Recode left Shark Tank India Season 2 without a deal after the sharks cited a conflict with Vineeta Singh's SUGAR, and later listed on the BSE SME exchange.
content:
Recode Studios sells makeup and cosmetics under its own label, online and through a network of franchise stores. It was co-founded by Rahul Sachdeva and Dheeraj Bansal.

Recode was one of the first pitches of Shark Tank India Season 2, in Episode 1. No shark invested. Namita Thapar and Aman Gupta pointed to the overlap with SUGAR Cosmetics, the brand run by fellow shark Vineeta Singh, and Peyush Bansal and Anupam Mittal were not convinced. Viewers criticised the sharks online, and Business Today covered the backlash.

The founders told afaqs that the episode brought marketplace and franchise enquiries. Recode listed on the BSE SME platform in May 2026. Its annual report for FY2025-26 shows revenue from operations of ₹79.95 crore, up from ₹47.80 crore the year before.

Recode is an example of a no-deal pitch that still produced lasting publicity, and of how a shark's own business can shape what the panel will fund.

faq.q: Did Recode get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: No. The sharks declined, citing a conflict with Vineeta Singh's SUGAR Cosmetics.
Yes. It listed on the BSE SME platform in May 2026.
Its FY2025-26 annual report shows revenue from operations of ₹79.95 crore.

faq.q: Where can I buy Recode makeup?
faq.a: On its website and in its franchise stores.

lessons: Sharks' own businesses can limit which categories they will fund; founders in crowded categories should plan for that.
A no-deal episode can still drive distribution enquiries if the brand is ready to take them.
Franchise stores gave the brand a growth route that did not depend on venture funding.
